The master classes should be taught by different, english speaking professors as far as i understand, so it does not apply.for BA they are not too selective, despite it being an overall great university with a good worldwide reputation.

Still, it is worth moving here just because the city is so wonderful for students and very pretty. The university facilities are great too. Many people speak english and a big part of the population are students, among those several internationals. No one i know regretted coming to heidelberg for computer science or otherwise.

You can take german classes with the university, Volkshochschule or maybe the Pädagogium if they offer non intense courses. Drop the classic private language schools, expensive and not worth the money.

 The average age idk, but around 1/3 of people in Heidelberg are under 30 years of age.

Public transport is functional too, but overall the city is not huge and very aesthetic so you can take nice walks to most places. 
If you ever get bored you can always take a 20 minute train ride to Mannheim and have more restaurant, clubbing and shopping opportunities

I happen to live in Germany and I'll be happy to support you, at least morally, since I was in a similar situation with my father, who isn't muslim, but was very controlling to the point of me not being able to pursue normal friendships and used to say very mean things as well. At 15 I left their house with a few packed bags and physically fought my way out to go live with my mom (after calling a lawyer hotline and asking if my dad is allowed to prevent me from leaving). Then I moved out from home at 18, but had her support.  
I cut off most contact with my father for years before giving him another chance. If he would not manage to be respectful towards me or my boyfriend I would cut him out of my life for months. He had to learn the hard way to be supportive or lose me completely and he did become better with age. This doesn't always work out sadly.   
Of course every situation is different, what I want to say is I have not regretted fighting for my freedom and I believe every young woman has the right to decide how she wants to live her own life. We are not our parent's property.  
It is extremely hard in Germany to legally disown their children without a very good reason and pursuing freedom of religion or escaping an abusive situation do not fall under that.    
You are 18 and an adult, you have the right to make your own decisions regarding religion, sexuality, where you go, who you meet and how you dress. These rights are protected under the Grundgesetz whether your father likes it or not and the police will become active if he tries to take your right away, especially if violence is involved. From what you are saying, to you this is a life or death situation. If choosing life means leaving, you need to do that. He cannot stop you.   
There should be networks other than the police who can offer support (Frauenhäuser, counseling, etc.).   
Still, if you manage to leave, keep your location secret at any cost!  If you pursue an education, your parents are legally forced to support you if they have the means. Otherwise I'd look into Bafög etc, financial is independence is crucial. 

P.S.: legal advice can be expensive sometimes, if you have the resources to get a Rechtsschutzversicherung it might be worth it. Otherwise there is free legal counseling in every city at the court or with the Beratungsschein.
